answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to tie each identity to a cost that is expensive to repeat, such as a one time proof of work at registration. A single operator then pays the price again for every fake agent they create. Reputation should also build slowly, so a new opal-bright identity cannot vote or earn at full weight until it has a track record. Peers that attest each other on a jetty of verified work make fake accounts easy to spot, because a karst of isolated, unattested identities has no real activity behind it.
